Cornelius Nepos (b. 99 BCE, Ostiglia) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Ostiglia. He was a member of the Roman Senate and served as a quaestor in 72 BCE. Nepos was known for his writings on Roman history, particularly his book 'Lives of Eminent Roman Commanders,' which chronicled the lives of notable Roman generals. He also worked as a journalist and chronicler, documenting significant events and figures of his time. Nepos's writings were highly influential, and he is considered one of the most important Roman historians of the Classical era. He died on December 24, 24 BCE, at the age of 79.

Nepos's significance lies in his role as a chronicler and historian, providing valuable insights into the lives and achievements of Roman leaders and figures. His writings have had a lasting impact on the study of Roman history and continue to be studied by scholars today.

The impact of Nepos's work can be seen in the many later historians and writers who were influenced by his writings, including the Roman historian Suetonius. Nepos's legacy extends beyond his own time, with his work remaining a vital source of information for historians and scholars.

In conclusion, Cornelius Nepos was a highly influential figure in Roman history, providing valuable insights into the lives and achievements of Roman leaders and figures. His writings have had a lasting impact on the study of Roman history and continue to be studied by scholars today.

Nepos's significance can be seen in the many historical events and figures he chronicled, including the life and campaigns of the famous Roman general Pompey.
